propositions: New noun-based bridge operations (preview, sync, status, pause, resume, check_access) must be exported as public library functions and registered as MCP tools with explicit typed inputs and no mode parameter
Legacy rebar.reconcile(mode=...) and bridge_fsck remain exported with unchanged defaults, signatures, return types, exceptions, and mutation boundaries to preserve backward compatibility

New library and MCP operations must reuse a shared typed result-bearing helper extracted beneath run_pass() that returns _Disposition and structured detail before _finish_disposition() converts to integer exit code
MCP allow_jira_sync gate must reject every mutating route (bridge_sync, pause, resume, legacy reconcile mutations) while permitting read-only operations (preview, status, fsck, check_access)

Each legacy reconcile mode must map to equivalent new bridge operation semantics via a shared mode policy (e.g., reconcile-check → bridge_preview, bootstrap-strict → bridge_sync with max_changes=10) without duplicating mode or exit-code tables
All new structured-result MCP tools must publish output schemas and remain in parity with library result types and generated references
